discussion.degradation_interpretation: FD004 strengthens the reliability argument at DEV stage and under controlled sensor degradation: most executable corruption scenarios retained positive selective gain. However, stuck-sensor corruption exposed the principal observed degradation failure mode.
discussion.main_interpretation: The evidence supports reliability-aware selective RUL prediction as a useful error-separation mechanism in some settings, but not as a universally improving policy. FD001 and FD002 produced positive held-out selective gains, whereas FD003 produced a genuine held-out negative result.
discussion.protocol_interpretation: FD004 also demonstrates that reliability evaluation depends on the admissibility of the underlying prediction protocol. The fixed 30-cycle input rule could not represent the full held-out endpoint population because 11 TEST trajectories were shorter than 30 cycles, so the frozen protocol required stopping before inference.

limitations.FD002_raw_target_gap: No genuine pre-existing FD002 raw-RUL final held-out authority was recovered. FD002 therefore contributes only its frozen piecewise-capped held-out result.
limitations.FD003_negative_generalization: FD003 is an important negative generalization result: the frozen policy slightly worsened accepted-set held-out MAE relative to the full TEST population.
limitations.FD004_short_history_limitation: The current fixed-length model protocol has no prospectively frozen mechanism for TEST histories shorter than 30 cycles. Padding, engine exclusion, row repetition, or variable-length inference were not introduced after TEST access.
limitations.FD004_stuck_sensor_limitation: All 16 negative selective-gain controlled-corruption scenarios in FD004 occurred in the stuck-sensor family, with failures concentrated most strongly at high severity.
limitations.absolute_mae_noncomparability: Do not rank datasets by absolute MAE. C-MAPSS subsets differ in operating conditions, fault structure, target conventions, and evaluation circumstances. Absolute MAEs are reported as dataset-specific outcomes, not as a pooled performance ranking.
limitations.evaluation_stage_separation: FD004 CLEAN DEV and corruption results are supporting evidence only and must not be presented as held-out TEST performance.
limitations.target_heterogeneity: Capped-target rows and raw/uncapped-target rows must remain explicitly distinguished. FD002 has no recovered raw-RUL final held-out authority, and FD004 has no scored held-out TEST MAE.

nonclaims: Do not claim that the selective policy improves every C-MAPSS subset.
Do not rank datasets by absolute MAE.
Do not treat capped and raw/uncapped target results as interchangeable.
Do not report an FD004 held-out TEST MAE.
Do not present FD004 DEV or corruption outcomes as held-out TEST outcomes.
Do not create a new FD002 raw-RUL score from stored endpoint predictions.
Do not retrofit padding or variable-length inference into the frozen FD004 primary TEST result.
recommended_table_notes: FD001 reports both its primary capped-RUL evaluation and its retained raw-RUL secondary analysis.
FD002 held-out results use the frozen piecewise-capped RUL target.
FD003 uses uncapped TRAIN-derived RUL and produced a negative held-out selective-MAE result.
FD004 held-out TEST was not scored because the frozen 30-cycle protocol was structurally incompatible with 11 of 248 TEST trajectories.
FD004 DEV/corruption results are reported separately as supporting evidence and are not substitutes for held-out TEST performance.

results.FD001: Selective filtering improved held-out TEST MAE under both the primary capped target and the retained raw-RUL secondary analysis, at relatively low realized coverage.
results.FD002: The frozen reliability policy improved held-out TEST MAE for the piecewise-capped RUL evaluation.
results.FD003: The frozen reliability policy did not improve held-out TEST MAE under the uncapped/raw RUL target; accepted MAE was slightly worse than full-population MAE.
results.FD004: No held-out TEST performance estimate is reported under the frozen protocol because short TEST trajectories made the complete endpoint population structurally inadmissible for the fixed 30-cycle input rule.
results.FD004_supporting_evidence: Before TEST access, FD004 CLEAN DEV showed positive selective MAE gain. Across 381 executable controlled-degradation scenarios, 365 showed positive selective gain; all 16 negative cases were in the stuck-sensor family, concentrated most strongly at high severity.
results.cross_dataset_summary: Reliability-aware selective prediction showed useful error separation in FD001 and FD002 and strong DEV/corruption evidence in FD004, but it did not generalize uniformly: FD003 produced a scored held-out negative result, and FD004 exposed a structural evaluation limitation of the fixed-window protocol.

table1_records.Interpretation: negative selective MAE gain; frozen reliability policy did not improve held-out TEST MAE
primary held-out TEST unscored because 11 TEST engines had fewer than the frozen 30 cycles required for one terminal input window; inference stopped before scoring
